# Thread

Threads of execution: starting, joining and detaching them, and asking about the current one.

## Installation

Add `Thread` to the `[Dependencies]` table of your package's `Rux.toml`:

```toml
[Dependencies]
Thread = { Namespace = "Rux", Version = "0.1.0" }
```

Standard packages are declared by hand: the registry does not serve them, so `rux add Rux/Thread` cannot add them.

## Dependencies

- [`Core`](/docs/api/core) 0.1.0
- [`FreeBSD`](/docs/api/freebsd) 0.1.0 (FreeBSD only)
- [`Linux`](/docs/api/linux) 0.1.0 (Linux only)
- [`macOS`](/docs/api/macos) 0.1.0 (macOS only)
- [`Memory`](/docs/api/memory) 0.1.0
- [`Windows`](/docs/api/windows) 0.1.0 (Windows only)

## Guide

### What it provides

| Module                                  | Covers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`Spawn`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#spawn) | [`Spawn`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#spawn), [`SpawnWith`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#spawn-with), [`ThreadOptions`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#thread-options) with a stack size, and [`JoinHandle<R>`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#join-handle) with [`Join`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#join) and [`Detach`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#detach) |
| `Current`                               | [`CurrentId`](/docs/api/thread/current#current-id), [`Yield`](/docs/api/thread/current#yield) and [`AvailableParallelism`](/docs/api/thread/current#available-parallelism)                                                                                                                                                |
| `Error`                                 | [`ThreadError`](/docs/api/thread/error#thread-error), why a thread could not be started                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

The module names describe where each declaration comes from; they are not part of an import path.

### Example

```rux
import Thread::Spawn;

func Square(value: uint64) -> uint64 {
    return value * value;
}

func Main() -> int {
    var handle = Spawn(Square, 12u64) catch { else => return 1 };
    return handle.Join() == 144u64 ? 0 : 2;
}
```

### Design

Rux has no closures, so a thread runs a function on a context value the caller moves to it, and leaves the function's result for whoever joins it. `Spawn(entry, context)` returns a [`JoinHandle<R>`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#join-handle); [`Join`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#join) waits for the thread and returns the result. The context and the result must be `Core::Sendable`, so neither can be a reference or hold an `Rc`. Dropping the handle, or calling [`Detach`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#detach), lets the thread run on and release itself when it finishes, destroying a result nobody took.

On Linux, FreeBSD and macOS threads are started with the C library's `pthread_create`, which gives each one its stack and its thread-local block, so a program that starts threads is linked against the C library. On Windows they are started with `CreateThread`. Each thread has its own copy of every `thread var`, starting at its initial value.

A panic on any thread ends the whole process, as it does on the main thread. Sharing data between threads takes an `Atomic<T>` or a lock from the `Sync` package; this package only starts and joins them.

## Index

### Types

| Name                                                     | Summary                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`ThreadError`](/docs/api/thread/error#thread-error)     | Why [`Spawn`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#spawn) could not start a thread. |
| [`ThreadOptions`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#thread-options) | How a thread is started: its stack size, for now.                     |
| [`JoinHandle<R>`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#join-handle)    | A started thread, and the result it will leave.                       |

### Functions

| Name                                                                     | Summary                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`CurrentId`](/docs/api/thread/current#current-id)                       | The calling thread's system-wide identifier.                                                               |
| [`Yield`](/docs/api/thread/current#yield)                                | Offers the processor to another thread that is ready to run, and returns when this one is scheduled again. |
| [`AvailableParallelism`](/docs/api/thread/current#available-parallelism) | How many threads can usefully run at once: the number of processors online, and at least one.              |
| [`Spawn<T, R>`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#spawn)                            | Starts a thread running `entry(context)` with the system's default stack size.                             |
| [`SpawnWith<T, R>`](/docs/api/thread/spawn#spawn-with)                   | Starts a thread running `entry(context)` as `options` say.                                                 |
